messages:
elaine_support: FYI got an urgent report from a customer using streaming tool-calls — their tool args arrive as partial JSON and the tool invocation fails mid-request. attaching minimal trace below.

elaine_support: Customer says it happens when they pause/resume their client (mobile app). They see JSON like: `{"tool":"search","args":{"query":"order 1234","metadata": ` (ends there). tool errors with malformed args.

elaine_support: Request id: rid_6f2b9c, endpoint: /v1/chat.stream, model: redwood-turbo-1, mode: tool-call streaming. Customer provided raw SSE chunks: 
```
data: {"event":"response.delta","delta":"{\"type\":\"tool_call\",\"name\":\"search\",\"arguments\": {\"query\": \"order 1234\", \"metadata\": "}

data: [DONE]
```

elaine_support: They said proxy sits in front of us (customer infra) but we see our ingress logs with a 502 around the same time and then a resumed connection where final bytes are missing.

elaine_support: Can eng reproduce or confirm if this is an ingress chunking/keepalive problem?

sam_irwin: looking. quick q: did the customer use websockets or SSE?

elaine_support: SSE. They used EventSource in their mobile wrapper.

sam_irwin: thanks. initial hypothesis: mid-stream pause + client reconnect -> proxy or LB combines/splits chunks and we end up with an open JSON tail (no closing brace) when we emit tool args as a streamed delta. I've seen this with strict Nginx proxy buffering + idle-timeout interactions.

sam_irwin: can you paste the raw request headers + any proxy via info from customer? need content-length/transfer-encoding and any keepalive settings.

elaine_support: customer sent these (redacted):
```
GET /v1/chat.stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Accept: text/event-stream
Connection: keep-alive
User-Agent: AcmeMobile/4.2
X-Request-ID: rid_6f2b9c
Proxy-Idle-Timeout: 30
```

elaine_support: They also sent their client-side EventSource logs showing a 2s freeze during network handoff.

sam_irwin: reproduced locally on staging by simulating a pause in the EventSource consumer. Repro steps:
1) curl to /v1/chat.stream with a small tool-call that streams arguments as deltas.
2) after first few SSE "data:" chunks, pause TCP read for 3000ms (tc qdisc/netem).
3) resume — server emits remaining deltas, but when proxy had buffering enabled, the trailing brace can be in a separate TCP packet that the proxy drops on resume if connection state changes.

sam_irwin: quick repro snippet (node):
```
const es = new EventSource(url);
es.onmessage = (m) => { if (m.data.includes('arguments')) { socket.pause(3000) } }
```

sam_irwin: Observed server-side log: `stream_write_partial(rid_6f2b9c): wrote 512 bytes, client stalled, write returned EPIPE on resume` then our SSE emitter sent `data: {"delta":"...\"metadata\":` and the final `}}` never reached the client.

alec_sre: adding infra notes — ingress uses envoy behind an L4 LB. Envoy has a 60s idle timeout and a downstream flush window. If downstream pauses, envoy can coalesce frames; on single-packet reassembly edgecases you can get chunk boundary shifts. I've seen similar with large HTTP/2 DATA frames split mid-json.

alec_sre: I ran a quick test toggling `strip_inbound_connection` and `flush_interval`. When `flush_interval` is 0 (aggressive flush per chunk) client received full JSON. With default coalescing, recreation of pause reproduced truncated tail.

sam_irwin: root cause hypothesis: our SSE emitter assumes continuous streaming and doesn't add chunk-level safe-guards (like an explicit end-of-object marker within the SSE payload). When proxies coalesce or split, a transient client pause can lead to the last bytes being delayed beyond a reconnect or causing the client to process an incomplete event.

sam_irwin: workaround we can ask customer to implement immediately: send a short keepalive event every 10s from client or set EventSource to buffer until double-newline, OR server-side we can wrap tool arguments in base64 payloads to avoid brace-splitting issues. Also recommend disabling aggressive proxy buffering on the customer's side (if possible).

elaine_support: customer asked for a hotfix — can we change server behavior to be more defensive?

alec_sre: low-risk mitigation we can ship from platform side: ensure SSE `data:` units that contain JSON arguments are emitted as complete, self-validating chunks by adding a small footer marker "__end__":true inside the streamed JSON object (internal-only marker we strip before tool invocation). That guarantees incomplete parse is detectable instead of silently failing.

sam_irwin: timeline: I can prepare a small patch today to annotate tool-call argument objects with the marker; on the emitter side we'll buffer until we see marker or timeout 200ms then abort and emit error event. Will open a PR against runtime.

alec_sre: parallel infra action: I'll add a recommendation to our public troubleshooting KB for customers running mobile/EventSource clients to set TLS upstream idle to > 60s and reduce proxy coalescing, and I'll add an envoy config experiment to staging to test safe flush modes.

ingest_bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2893 — assigned to eng-runtime (sam_irwin) and eng-sre (alec_sre). Severity: P2.

elaine_support: thanks — I'll escalate to the customer with two items: 1) immediate client workaround (keepalive + buffer settings) 2) we'll deploy defensive emitter patch and update timeline.

sam_irwin: PR will reference rid_6f2b9c and include unit tests + small repro harness. ETA initial patch in 6h, staging rollout EOD.

elaine_support: perfect. I'll follow up on customer thread and close once staging verifies. :thumbsup:
